rationale: Sets the standard of conduct staff acknowledge. The criterion also expects deviations to be addressed, which the disciplinary and reporting controls cover.
Shows deviations from the code of conduct are addressed in a timely and consistent way.
A documented, consistently applied discipline process is how accountability for control duties is enforced.
Documents reporting lines and authorities. The criterion also expects board oversight of the structure.
A named security officer is the delegated authority for the program.
Gives accountability for the program a single owner. Performance measures for individuals sit in HR controls.
The oversight body and its minutes are the core evidence for board independence and oversight of internal control.
Management review is what reaches the board or executives. It does not show independence of the oversight body.
The forum where control deficiencies are communicated to those who can correct them.
A named owner is who is held accountable when a control fails.
Assigned control owners show responsibilities are delegated to named people.
Stated service commitments and system requirements are the objectives risk assessment works against.
The assessment uses the stated objectives. It does not by itself prove they are clear.
The annual assessment is how risks across the entity are identified and analyzed.
The register records each identified risk, its rating and who owns it.
Treatment decisions on the register show which risks controls are selected to mitigate.
Treatment plans show analyzed risks lead to action.
Treatment of disruption risks is where mitigation activities are chosen and tracked. Business impact analysis needs the continuity controls.
Fraud and insider threat consideration is the criterion's subject: incentives, opportunity, and management override.
A risk review triggered by significant change is what the criterion asks for.
Links each risk to the controls that mitigate it, which shows controls were chosen against risk.
Shows which general technology controls cover which systems. It does not show the controls operate.
The policy suite is where expectations are set for each control area.
Annual review keeps policies in line with how the organization works. Procedures that put policies into action are separate controls.
Ongoing evaluation of whether controls are present and functioning is the criterion's subject.
An independent penetration test is a separate evaluation of technical controls. It covers a subset of the system.
Finds exploitable weaknesses that scanning misses. Continuous detection is covered by vulnerability management.
A separate evaluation by someone independent of the control owners.
Tracking deficiencies to closure is how they are communicated to those who correct them.
Knowing which obligations apply is the start of communicating with external parties. Stakeholder communication is covered by the external commitment controls.
Policies and acknowledgements show expectations were communicated to staff.
A reporting channel lets staff raise control failures upward.
Gives customers and others a way to tell the entity about incidents.
A confidential reporting path supports ethical conduct when the management line is part of the concern.
An alternative internal channel for raising concerns.
Published commitments are the entity's communication to customers about its controls.
Tells customers how and when they will hear about incidents.
Screening before hire supports a commitment to integrity.
The criterion lists considering the background of individuals. Competence checks and development are covered elsewhere.
Training develops competence. Attendance alone does not show competence.
Training is how security responsibilities are communicated to staff.
Defining what each role requires is where competence starts.
Onboarding is where agreements, training and policies are completed.
Access is requested and approved as part of joining.
Access is removed when employment ends.
Removal at departure is part of modifying and removing access.
Agreements set expectations of conduct. A conduct program is covered by the ethics controls.
Confidentiality agreements bind staff to protect confidential information. Identifying and classifying it is covered by the data controls.
Reviews keep competence maintained rather than assumed.
Performance reviews are where accountability for control duties is reinforced.
Contractors need registering and authorizing like employees.
Contractors are third parties with access.
One identity provider enforces access policy in one place.
Multi factor authentication is a core logical access protection. It is one of several.
A password baseline protects accounts where stronger factors are unavailable.
Gives credentials that cannot use single sign on a controlled home.
Role based access limits who can reach protected assets.
Role based access and least privilege are what authorizing access by role means.
Approved requests are the authorization the criterion requires before access is granted.
Approval of changes to access, not only of new access.
Removes credentials when authorization ends.
Timely removal is the removal half of modifying or removing access.
Periodic review confirms registered users are still authorized.
Access reviews are how role based access is checked as roles change.
Privileged access needs tighter approval and review than standard access.
Separating duties is part of authorizing access on the basis of responsibilities.
Machine credentials are protected assets of the access architecture.
Service accounts need the same authorization and review as people.
Session limits bound how long a stolen session is useful.
Encryption at rest protects data if storage is exposed. It is one of the access protections.
Encryption in transit protects information while it moves. Authorizing who may send it is separate.
Encryption is only as strong as its key management.
A managed secret store protects credentials the system depends on.
Segmentation limits what a compromised host can reach.
Limits traffic between networks, and between the outside and inner tiers.
Default deny firewall rules are a core boundary protection against outside threats.
Keeps management interfaces off the public internet.
Filters attack traffic from outside the system boundary.
Remote access through verified identity and device rather than network location.
Detects malicious activity in the cloud control plane.
Monitors system components for anomalies. Routing and response are covered by alerting controls.
Hardened baselines reduce what an attacker can reach.
A baseline gives configuration drift something to be measured against.
Disk encryption protects data on devices that leave the premises.
Encryption makes recovery of data from disposed devices impractical. It does not replace sanitization.
Protects data on portable devices and media. It does not authorize transfers.
Endpoint protection is the primary control for malicious software on devices.
Enrollment is what makes remote lock and wipe possible. It is not proof a wipe happened.
Management enforces protection settings across devices.
Patching removes the vulnerabilities malicious software uses.
Patching is how found vulnerabilities are treated. Finding them is covered by scanning.
Remote wipe removes data from a device that cannot be recovered. The capability alone does not show it was used.
Automatic screen lock means physical proximity is not enough to use a device.
Classification is how confidential information is identified. Maintaining the inventory is a separate control.
A data inventory is how confidential information is identified and kept track of.
The retention schedule sets when confidential information is disposed of.
A retention schedule enforced technically is how personal information is kept no longer than needed.
Secure disposal is the criterion's subject.
Disposal that makes data unrecoverable is what the criterion asks for before protections end.
Secure disposal of personal information, across copies and vendors.
Keeps confidential data out of environments with weaker protection.
The privacy notice and its updates are the criterion's subject.
Consent and choice records show choices were communicated and respected.
Consent is captured before collection. The criterion also expects the consequences of declining to be communicated.
Collecting only what is needed is how collection stays consistent with privacy objectives.
Limiting use to disclosed purposes is the criterion's subject.
Handling access requests from authenticated data subjects is the criterion's subject.
Access responses must also include disclosure accounting, which a holdings only response does not.
Correction requests and passing corrections to third parties are the criterion's subject.
Reactive correction is part of keeping data accurate. Proactive quality checks are also expected.
Governing disclosures shows each one matches the notice and consent. Subprocessors are covered separately.
The disclosure record is the criterion's subject.
A record of unauthorized disclosures, including near misses, is the criterion's subject.
Agreements hold vendors to privacy commitments. Periodic assessment of vendors is also needed.
Data processing agreements bind vendors who handle personal data.
Contract terms commit vendors to notify. Receipt and response need operating records.
Deciding who is notified and when, before an incident, is the criterion's subject.
A channel for inquiries, complaints and disputes, and evidence they are resolved.
Peer review is how changes are approved before they are implemented. Authorization, testing and deployment are covered by the other change controls.
Automated tests are the testing step of the change process.
Tests show processing logic behaves as specified. They do not prove production processing.
Separate environments give changes somewhere to be tested before production.
Change authorization and approval is the criterion's core: changes are authorized, tested and approved before implementation.
Covers changes that bypass the normal path, so the criterion holds in an emergency.
The documented lifecycle is where the change process is defined.
Dependency scanning finds known vulnerable components before they ship.
Finds newly disclosed vulnerabilities in dependencies.
A committed credential is a failure to protect credentials.
A secret in a change is a vulnerability that change introduced.
Validation at ingestion controls what enters the system. Completeness and duplicate handling also need checking.
A processing specification defines what accurate means. Communicating it to stakeholders is also needed.
Reconciling outputs to inputs shows processing was complete and accurate.
Monitoring shows outputs were produced. Delivery to the right recipient needs its own check.
Integrity of intermediate stores. Retention and retry behavior also matter.
Retained logs are the input to anomaly monitoring and investigation.
Logs are information used to run internal control. Their quality depends on completeness.
An inventory is quality information about what the controls apply to.
The criterion starts with the inventory of information assets.
Alerting on anomalies is the criterion's subject.
An alert only helps if someone receives it.
An on call rotation staffs incident response.
A defined cadence of vulnerability discovery and remediation is the criterion's detection and monitoring.
Detects configuration changes that introduce vulnerabilities.
Evaluating security events to decide whether they are incidents is the criterion's subject.
The incident response plan is the program the criterion asks to be executed.
Postmortems show how incidents were understood and remediated.
Lessons and actions from recovery.
An exercise is operating evidence the plan works when no incident has occurred.
Recovery procedures are the criterion's subject.
Continuity planning is a mitigation for business disruption.
The continuity plan covers recovery infrastructure. Environmental protections are separate.
Capacity monitoring and planning is the criterion's subject.
Backups are a recovery protection. Environmental protections are separate.
Backups mitigate loss from disruption.
Restore testing is the criterion's subject.
The vendor register is the population third party risk management works from.
Due diligence scaled to risk is how vendor risk is assessed and managed.
Detects vendors adopted outside procurement so they can be assessed.
Subprocessors are vendors that receive customer data.
Disclosure to a subprocessor needs the consent or notice the criterion asks for.
Subprocessors are third parties that must meet privacy commitments.
Where a cloud provider runs the facility, reviewing their report is how physical access is evidenced.
The provider is a vendor whose controls the entity relies on.
Covers offices in scope. Data centers are covered by the provider review.
Vendor assessment covers privacy commitments where the vendor handles personal information.
Controls how approved changes reach production, which is the implementation step of the change process.
Lets each change be followed from request to release, which is how an auditor samples the whole change process.
